discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Good catch — the code fixtures all carried "overloaded" in the message, so the code check was not covered on its own. Added table-driven cases for each capacity code with a neutral message, plus an unknown code with a neutral message that must stay non-retryable.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. I removed the cap. Each failure record is what stops its run from falling back to an earlier checkpoint, so failures now persist for the life of the session, as checkpoint history does. Covered by `keeps every failure so no failed run falls back to an earlier checkpoint` in `checkpoint-records.test.ts`; it fails if the cap is put back.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch, fixed. The test now starts waiting before the tracked start rejects and asserts the waiter resolves. I confirmed it fails against a version that tracks the raw start promise, where a failed start rejects existing waiters, and passes against the real implementation.

Valid, fixed in 90df99574b. `applyCanonicalHistory` now returns `withLivePluginIssues(sessionMessages, historyMessages)`, which carries the session's live plugin-warning lines (`meta.messageKind: "plugin_issue"`) into the saved history, each inserted at its original position by `createdAt`. It also skips any line whose id is already in history. Tests: the hook test now finishes a queued turn so the reconcile path replaces the transcript with saved history that has no warnings. It asserts the saved answer is applied and both the start warning and the streamed notice are still there, and it fails without the change. Unit tests in history-reconciliation.test.ts cover ordering and the no-warnings case (history is returned unchanged). Residual: the warnings aren't persisted, so reopening the session later from history (a fresh hydrate) won't show them. The start-of-session information is gone at that point, and a new session reports any plugin that still fails.
